newsitem.title: EU: EP DEBATES COUNCIL COMMON POSITION ON SUMMERTIME.
newsitem.headline: EP DEBATES COUNCIL COMMON POSITION ON SUMMERTIME.

text.p: EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT SESSION NEWS PRESS RELEASE
Summertime Co-decision procedure - second reading. 314 votes
required for amendments to be adopted. (A4-180/97 - Bellere)

Tuesday, 10 June - Spalato Bellere (I, Ind) came before the House to recommend approval of a Council common position which means that the member states will change over to summertime and back again on the same date. It does not, however, imply harmonisation of summertime throughout the EU. Mr Bellere explained that the previous experience of summertime, under which countries in the South of the EU enjoyed an extra hour of daylight had been extremely beneficial with considerable energy-savings achieved in, for example, Italy. The agreement, however, provides under the subsidiarity principle for the decision on which time to follow to be taken by the member states and, as Florus Wijsenbeek (NL, ELDR) pointed out, this at present results in 4 pm European time applying to mainland Continental countries, translating to 3 pm in Britain and Ireland and 5 pm in other countries such as Greece and Finland. As he put it, this did not create a particular problem as long as changes were made on the same date each year.

Replying for the Commission, Neil Kinnock, emphasised that transport companies had been anxiously waiting for the agreement in order to print new timetables and that it would be important for the future with applicant countries already following EU guidelines.
